title: The Second-Derivative Test
quickIdea: At a stationary point, f'' > 0 means the curve bends up (minimum) and f'' < 0 means it bends down (maximum). f'' = 0 decides nothing.
remember: Suppose f'(c) = 0 and f'' is continuous near c. If f''(c) > 0 then f has a local minimum at c; if f''(c) < 0 then a local maximum.
If f''(c) = 0 the test is inconclusive: the point may be a minimum (x^4 at 0), a maximum (-x^4 at 0) or neither (x^3 at 0).
The test needs f'(c) = 0 first; applying it where f' does not vanish is meaningless.
The test is one-sided in a second sense: it is silent at points where f' fails to exist, so it cannot handle |x| at 0.
It is the fastest classifier for a cubic: f'' at the two stationary points has opposite signs, so a cubic with two stationary points has one maximum and one minimum.

example.prompt: GATE CSE 2023 Q.18: classify the stationary points of f(x) = x^3 + 15x^2 - 33x - 36.
example.work: f'(x) = 3x^2 + 30x - 33 = 3(x^2 + 10x - 11) = 3(x + 11)(x - 1), so the stationary points are -11 and 1. f''(x) = 6x + 30. At x = 1, f''(1) = 36 > 0, a local minimum. At x = -11, f''(-11) = -36 < 0, a local maximum.
example.answer: A local maximum at x = -11 and a local minimum at x = 1, so the true statements are 'f has a local maximum' and 'f has a local minimum'.

gateAngle: The second-derivative test is the classifier GATE expects you to reach for on a cubic, and 2023 Q.18 is a pure instance. The exam also tests the inconclusive case: 2008 Q.25 has f''(2) = 0, and the answer depends on noticing that the test has failed rather than on applying it.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2023 Q.18: for f(x) = x^3 + 15x^2 - 33x - 36, which statements hold?
variations.answer: f has a local maximum (at -11) and f has a local minimum (at 1).
variations.why: Two stationary points, opposite signs of f'', so exactly one of each.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: For f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 4, find and classify the stationary points.
variations.answer: Local maximum at x = 0 with f(0) = 4, local minimum at x = 2 with f(2) = 0. f'(x) = 3x(x - 2), f''(x) = 6x - 6, f''(0) = -6 < 0 and f''(2) = 6 > 0.
variations.why: The same two-step procedure with smaller numbers, so the arithmetic cannot hide a missing sign check.

trap.why: A zero second derivative only means this test cannot decide; the point can still be a minimum, a maximum or neither.
trap.counterexample: x^4 has f''(0) = 0 and a minimum at 0; x^3 has f''(0) = 0 and no extremum at 0. The same value of f'' gives opposite verdicts.

check.question: f(x) = x^4 - 2x^2. Classify its stationary points.
check.answer: Local maximum at 0, local minima at x = 1 and x = -1.
